To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bromfenac  0.09% is an effective adjunctive treatment for reducing inflammation after cataract extraction in patients with pseudo exfoliation syndrome, and that the incidence of cystoidal macular edema was reduced in patients with pseudo-exfoliation syndrome treated with bromfenac ophthalmicsolution.
(1) bromfenac  is effective in reducing anterior segment postoperative inflammation in eyes with pseudoexfoliative glaucoma (PXG), and (2) bromfenac has no effect on the incidence of CME.

(1) bromfenac ophthalmicsolution 0.09%, when used in combination with a topical steroid after cataract surgery in patients with pseudo-exfoliation syndrome, reduces the incidence of anterior segment inflammation; and (2) the addition of bromfenac ophthamicsolution 0,09% did not increase the incidence of postoperative cystoid macular oedema.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NSAIDs in the management of CME.
the role of bromefenac as an adjunctive to steroid treatment after cataract extraction and IOL implantation in eyes with pseudoexfoliative syndrome.
the use of non-steroidals in reducing inflammation in eyes with pseudoexfoliative material after cataract extraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bromfenac is an effective adjuvant to reduce the inflammation seen with PXF after cataract extraction and intraocular lens (IOL) implantation.
bromfenac ophthalmicsolution 0.09%, in addition to topical steroids, reduces inflammation after cataract extraction in PXF eyes.
bromfenac is an adjunctive therapy that reduces anterior segment inflammation in PXF after cataract.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bromfenac ophthalmicsolution 0.09%, as an adjunctive treatment to topical corticosteroids, can reduce anterior segment inflammation after cataract surgery in patients with PXF.
the use of bromfenac ophthalmicsolution 0.09%, when added to topical steroids after surgery for cataract, reduces anterior chamber inflammation in patients with PXF.
the use of a topical NSAID as an adjunct to a steroid regimen is beneficial in patients with PXF after cataract extraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bromfenac is a good choice of NSAID in the postoperative setting, and that we should consider adding it to our treatment regimen.
the use of bromfenac ophthalmicsolution 0.09%, as adjunctive therapy to dexamethasome 0.1%, after cataract surgery is safe and well tolerated.
bromfenac is a safe and effective adjunct to topical steroids for the management of postoperative inflammation after cataract extraction in patients with PXF.
